<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only sources the PKGBUILD file and evaluates top-level definitions; it never runs `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`. The top level consists solely of variable assignments (`pkgname`, `_pkgname`, `pkgver`, and others), the `source` and `sha256sums` fields, and the declaration of the `package()` function. None of these lines invoke `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or any other command that could reach the internet or execute code. The `source` variable points to the upstream release tarball on GitHub (`https://github.com/methamphetaminelab/gramtty/releases/download/v1.0.1/gramtty-1.0.1-x86_64-linux.tar.gz`), which is the intended upstream artifact and is fetched automatically by `makepkg` only when needed (outside the `--printsrcinfo` mode). Because no executable code is triggered while the file is sourced, there is no risk of data exfiltration or backdoor installation. Thus, sourcing/parsing this PKGBUILD with `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is harmless and introduces no supply-chain concerns.
  </details>
  <evidence>
  </evidence>
  <summary>Top-level only sets vars and source; no code runs when sourcing.</summary>
</security_assessment>
